# container-deploy contract

Contract version: `1.0`

The `container-deploy` category defines 2 capabilities: 1 required and 1 optional. An adapter implementing this category must provide every required capability; a command that needs an optional capability the resolved adapter lacks uses the capability's fallback when one is named.

## Capabilities

| Capability | Required | Side effect | Inputs | Outputs | Fallback | Added in minor | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container-deploy.deploy` | required | yes | `target`, `image` | `status`, `url` | - | - | Build and deploy a container workload to its target environment. |
| `container-deploy.build-image` | optional | yes | `context`, `tag` | `status`, `image` | - | - | Build a container image from the project's build context (and optionally push it to a registry). A real side effect: disk writes to the local image store, and possibly a network push to a remote registry. |

## Details

### container-deploy.deploy

Build and deploy a container workload to its target environment.

- Status: required
- Side effect: yes
- Inputs: `target`, `image`
- Outputs: `status`, `url`
- Fallback: none

### container-deploy.build-image

Build a container image from the project's build context (and optionally push it to a registry). A real side effect: disk writes to the local image store, and possibly a network push to a remote registry.

- Status: optional
- Side effect: yes
- Inputs: `context`, `tag`
- Outputs: `status`, `image`
- Fallback: none
